feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and overpacked, which reduces impact and makes the structure feel less streamlined than it could be.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing leadership, scope, and responsibility over time.  
- Good use of scale and credibility markers: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Strong alignment between headline, competencies, experience, and technical skills; the profile is consistent and targeted.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, footer projects, and role bullets; consolidate to sharpen focus and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond activity descriptions (e.g., traffic growth, engagement lift, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption improvements).  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; punctuation/hyphenation varies (“organization wide” should be “organization-wide” if used adjectivally); title casing is inconsistent (“Coleman DAVIS” vs standard capitalization). No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and foreground scale/impact: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading public-sector web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume communications.”
- Replace the generic “building the platforms” phrasing with stronger action verbs like “leading,” “modernizing,” or “scaling.”
- Consider a sharper second sentence: “Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics ecosystems, editorial workflows, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled search/content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Standardize style: use either “AI-enabled search and content experiences” or “AI-enabled user experiences,” but align with the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models/content operations” and the capability list substantially repeat the subtitle and Core Competencies section.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with both Recent Projects and Topline Skills; “AI-enabled search/content experiences” would be more specific.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the target roles, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and shorten longer items for cleaner readability.
- Replace broad terms like “operations” where possible with more specific capability language.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream delivery
- If space allows, order by strongest differentiators first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” repeat the header and Topline Skills almost verbatim.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and recent NACo experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a short lead-in such as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action verbs and style: e.g., “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched,” “Produced.”
- Replace vague phrases like “improve discovery” and “designed for continued campaign growth” with specific outcomes, scale, or purpose if available.
- Standardize formatting and punctuation; spell out “10 × 20-foot” consistently and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for smoother phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series closely overlap with current and past NACo role bullets.
- The anniversary campaign adds fresher differentiation; prioritize projects not already well covered elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consulting-level outcomes, transformation work, and the newest/highest-value initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client impact: “Advise a national U.S. membership association on digital strategy, enterprise web improvement, and communications operations across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Consolidate execution bullets: combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on improving coordination, publishing efficiency, or decision-making.
- Emphasize 2–3 standout contributions only: Drupal campaign/microsite builds, enterprise CMS/front-end support, and AI-enabled search strategy.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, reduced publishing time, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats themes from Director of Digital Media; frame this as consultant advisory/implementation instead.
- Drupal microsites and AI search also appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest platform metrics into one bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused: add growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten remaining bullets with action/result phrasing: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…,” “Expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making,” “Established governance and publishing standards to streamline cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-programming language may duplicate earlier weekly video/livestream experience unless this version emphasizes the studio build and organizational scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to the step-up in responsibility: channel operations, editorial coordination, and repeatable advocacy formats.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct outcomes:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and publishing consistency.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve efficiency and content quality.
- If possible, add metrics: email open/click rates, video cadence/views, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership verbs.
- Avoid repeating “weekly video updates” language too closely from the 2015–2018 role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies and reads generic rather than differentiated. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content operations” or “content strategy” to better match recent leadership roles.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “messaging,” “planning,” and “leadership” styles.
- If space allows, make one item more distinctive, e.g. “Enterprise web and communications governance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is required for target roles.
- Keep only platforms most supported by recent experience; if SharePoint/Power Pages are not evidenced in recent roles, move them to Technical + IT only.
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Public-sector web platform delivery” is stronger than just “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; Topline Skills should stay strategic, not exhaustive.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; consider keeping it in one place only.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g.: “Analytics infrastructure, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools here; move the full stack to Technical + IT. Suggested version: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO and performance analysis”
- Consider tightening the title to “Analytics & Performance Optimization” for clarity and punch.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one measurable proof point tied to recent work, such as supporting “3.5M annual page views” or analytics for a “10,000+ page” migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure.”
- Tool list also overlaps almost exactly with “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep this section higher-level.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and recent in-house studio/event delivery impact rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to outcomes/capability: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to match Director-level experience.
- Consider adding scale if accurate: “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy programming, conferences, and recurring multimedia series.”
- If space allows, group related items for concision: “Studio operations, PTZ camera systems, and multi-camera livestream workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- “PTZ camera systems” is very tool-specific compared with the rest of the CV; keep only if targeting hands-on production roles.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use **GitHub Pages** only if you’ve actively built/deployed with it; otherwise remove it as the least strategic item.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or making one more strategic and this one more tool-specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overlisting it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tooling rather than basic coding terms alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to capability-led phrasing: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers unless required: use “HTML, CSS” instead of “HTML5, CSS3” for a cleaner, more senior presentation.
- Consider replacing “Google Tag Manager” with “Tag management (Google Tag Manager)” to group it as a function, not just a product.
- If accurate, add light scope/impact via label wording: “lightweight front-end development,” “technical troubleshooting,” or “web implementation support” to match the consultant/director roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid adding similar automation language here unless it is specifically code/deployment-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most differentiating tools first; if Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier are the real automation stack, lead with those and de-emphasize commodity collaboration tools.
- Consider trimming to the tools you actively used to build systems, e.g. “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana,” unless Slack/Teams are required by the role.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to outcomes instead of listing tools alone, e.g. “Built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” is already stated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Slack and Teams add little differentiation unless collaboration platforms are specifically relevant to target roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Because email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope rather than more tools: **Enterprise email campaign delivery, newsletter operations, segmentation and member communications**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, order by recency/relevance rather than alphabetically

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating newsletter reach or channel leadership here; that impact is already covered in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 NACo roles.
- “Engagement” may overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already evidenced in the recent Director role. This item should be tightened to emphasize optimization capability, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Tag Manager • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Replace vague **Dashboarding** with outcome-oriented **KPI reporting** or **executive reporting**
- If accurate, add one higher-value capability over a generic term, e.g. **funnel analysis**, **conversion tracking**, or **data visualization**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping platforms here and moving broader capabilities there.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already called out in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid expanding this into a second full analytics summary.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more concrete, emphasize “firsts” and team-building, and add any measurable outputs if available.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and video.”
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, expanding in-house multimedia capacity.”
- Clarify management scope: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if possible: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social performance, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/building the capability, not scaling it.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple NACo entries; specify early-stage team/process setup here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles. Emphasize the “first podcast” achievement and tighten the policy/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and policy-support projects for NACo programs while expanding the organization’s early digital content capabilities.”
- Replace vague phrasing with clearer ownership: “Produced multimedia and digital content for program and policy initiatives, including planning, scripting and production support.”
- Make the podcast launch the final, strongest clause: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one metric or scope point: number of episodes, audience, programs supported, or types of research/projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry lighter and more foundational.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here since those strengths are better established in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only or framed more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production Tools**
- Rewrite as: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast production workflows • Livestream studio operations**
- Keep naming consistent with other technical sections by listing tools/platforms first, then operational capabilities.
- If possible, add specificity elsewhere in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., broadcast-quality studio, recurring video series, or podcast launch outcomes.
